source_text: Τὸ τοῦ λιμοῦ πάθος κατηνάγκασε πολλοὺς πολλάκις καὶ τοὺς ὅρους κινῆσαι τῆς φύσεως· ἅψασθαι μὲν ἄνθρωπον τῶν ὁμοφύλων σωμάτων, μητέρα δὲ παῖδα, ὃν ἐκ τῆς γαστρὸς προήγαγε, πάλιν τῇ γαστρὶ κακῶς ὑποδέξασθαι. Καὶ τοῦτο τὸ δρᾶμα Ἰουδαϊκὴ ἐτραγῴδησεν ἱστορία, ἣν Ἰώσηπος ἡμῖν ὁ σπουδαῖος συνεγράψατο, ὅτε τὰ δεινὰ πάθη τοὺς Ἱεροσολυμίτας κατέλαβε, τῆς εἰς τὸν Κύριον δυσσεβείας ἐνδίκους τιμωρίας τιννύντας. Ὁρᾷς καὶ αὐτὸν τὸν ἡμέτερον Θεὸν τὰ μὲν ἄλλα τῶν παθῶν πολλάκις παρατρέχοντα, ἐπὶ δὲ τοῖς πεινῶσι συμπαθῶς σπλαγχνιζόμενον· Σπλαγχνίζο μαι γὰρ, φησὶν, ἐπὶ τὸν ὄχλον. Διὸ καὶ ἐν τῇ τελευταίᾳ κρίσει, ἔνθα προσκαλεῖται τοὺς δικαίους ὁ Κύριος, τὴν πρώτην τάξιν ὁ μεταδοτικὸς ἐπέχει· ὁ τροφεὺς πρωτοστάτης τῶν τιμωμένων· ὁ τὸν ἄρτον χορηγήσας πρὸ πάντων καλεῖται· ὁ χρηστὸς καὶ εὐμετάδοτος πρὸ τῶν ἄλλων δικαίων τῇ ζωῇ παραπέμπεται. Ὁ ἀκοινώνητος καὶ φειδωλὸς πρὸ πάντων ἁμαρτωλῶν τῷ πυρὶ παραδίδοται. Ἐπὶ τὴν μητέρα σε τῶν ἐντολῶν ὁ καιρὸς καλεῖ· καὶ σφόδρα μερίμνησον, ἵνα σε μὴ παρέλθῃ ὁ τῆς πανηγύρεως καὶ τῶν συναλλαγμάτων καιρός. Ῥεῖ γὰρ ὁ χρόνος, καὶ οὐκ ἐκδέχεται τὸν βραδύνοντα· ἐπείγονται αἱ ἡμέ ραι, τὸν ὀκνηρὸν παρατρέχουσιν. Καὶ ὡς οὐκ ἔστι ῥεῦμα ποταμοῦ στῆσαι, εἰ μή τις, κατὰ τὴν πρώτην ἔντευξιν καὶ προσβολὴν ἀνελόμενος, εἰς δέον τῷ ὕδατι χρήσαιτο· οὕτως οὐδὲ τὸν χρόνον ταῖς ἀναγκαστικαῖς περιόδοις ἐλαυνόμενον ἐπισχεῖν, οὐδὲ παρ ελθόντα ἀναλῦσαι εἰς τὸ κατόπιν, εἰ μή τις προσάγοντος λάβοιτο. Καὶ διὰ τοῦτο τὴν ἐντολὴν ὡς φεύγουσαν κάτασχε καὶ ἐπιτέλεσον, καὶ λαβόμενος πανταχόθεν ἐν ταῖς ἀγκάλαις περίδραξαι. Δὸς ὀλίγα, καὶ πολλὰ κτῆσαι· λῦσον τὴν πρωτότυπον ἁμαρ τίαν τῇ τῆς τροφῆς μεταδόσει. Ὡς γὰρ Ἀδὰμ, κακῶς φαγὼν, τὴν ἁμαρτίαν παρέπεμψεν, οὕτως ἐξαλείφομεν ἡμεῖς τὴν ἐπίβουλον βρῶσιν, ἐὰν χρείαν ἀδελφοῦ καὶ λιμὸν θεραπεύσωμεν. Λαοὶ, ἀκούσατε· Χριστιανοὶ, ἐνωτίσασθε· ὅτι τάδε λέγει Κύριος, οὐ δημηγορῶν αὐτοφώνως. τοῖς δὲ τῶν δούλων στόμασιν ἐνηχῶν ὡς ὀργάνοις. Μὴ φανῶμεν οἱ λογικοὶ τῶν ἀλόγων ὠμότεροι. Ἐκεῖνα γὰρ τοῖς ἐκ τῆς γῆς φυομένοις παρὰ τῆς φύσεως ὡς κοινῇ κέχρηνται. Καὶ προβάτων ἀγέλαι ἓν καὶ τὸ αὐτὸ καταβόσκονται ὄρος· ἵπποι δὲ παμπληθεῖς μίαν καὶ τὴν αὐτὴν κατανέμονται πεδιάδα· καὶ πάντα τὰ καθ' ἕκαστον οὕτως ἀλλήλοις ἀντιπαραχωρεῖ τῆς ἀναγκαίας τῶν χρειῶν ἀπολαύσεως· ἡμεῖς δὲ, ἐγκολπιζόμεθα τὰ κοινὰ, τὰ τῶν πολλῶν μόνοι ἔχομεν. Αἰδεσθῶμεν Ἑλλήνων φιλάνθρωπα διηγήματα. Παρά τισιν ἐκείνων νόμος φιλάνθρωπος μίαν τράπεζαν, καὶ κοινὰ τὰ σιτία, μίαν ἑστίαν σχεδὸν τὸν πολυάνθρωπον δῆμον ἀπεργάζεται. Καταλείψωμεν τοὺς ἔξωθεν, καὶ ἐπέλθωμεν τὸ τῶν τρισ χιλίων ὑπόδειγμα· τὸ πρῶτον τῶν Χριστιανῶν ζηλώσωμεν σύνταγμα· ὅπως ἦν αὐτοῖς ἅπαντα κοινὰ, ὁ βίος, ἡ ψυχὴ, ἡ συμφωνία, ἡ τράπεζα κοινὴ, ἀδιαίρετος ἀδελφότης, ἀγάπη ἀνυπόκριτος, τὰ πολ λὰ σώματα ἓν ἐργαζομένη· τὰς διαφόρους ψυχὰς εἰς μίαν ὁμόνοιαν ἁρμόζουσα. Πολλὰ τῆς φιλαδελ φίας ἔχεις ἐκ Παλαιᾶς Διαθήκης καὶ ἐκ τῆς Νέας τὰ ὑποδείγματα. Πρεσβύτην ἐὰν ἴδῃς λιμώττοντα, μετά στειλαι καὶ θρέψον, ὡς Ἰωσὴφ τὸν Ἰακώβ. Ἐχθρὸνἐὰν εὕρῃς στενούμενον, μὴ ἐπιβάλῃς τῇ ὀργῇ τῇ κατ εχούσῃ τὴν ἄμυναν· ἀλλὰ θρέψον ὡς ἐκεῖνος τοὺς ἀδελφοὺς τοὺς πωλήσαντας.
thought_title: Famine's unnatural horrors and the call to seize the time for mercy
orientation: Basil is preaching to his congregation during a famine, having just described the physical devastation of starvation; he now turns to the unnatural acts famine forces, the judgment that awaits the unmerciful, and the urgent call to give.
pass_a_gloss: The suffering of famine has often compelled many even to move the boundaries of nature: for a human being to touch the bodies of his own kind, and a mother to receive back badly into her belly the child whom she brought forth from her womb. And this drama Jewish history acted out as a tragedy, which Josephus the diligent wrote down for us, when the terrible sufferings seized the people of Jerusalem, as they were paying the just punishments for their impiety toward the Lord. You see that our God himself often passes over the other sufferings, but is moved with compassion in his bowels for those who hunger; for I am moved with compassion, he says, for the crowd. Therefore also in the last judgment, where the Lord summons the righteous, the generous person holds the first rank; the nourisher is the foremost of those being honored; the one who supplied bread is called before all; the good and freely-sharing person is sent on to life before the other righteous. The selfish and stingy person is handed over to the fire before all sinners. The season calls you to the mother of the commandments; and be very anxious, lest the season of the festal assembly and of reconciliations pass you by. For time flows, and does not wait for the one who delays; the days press on, they run past the sluggish one. And just as it is not possible to stop the stream of a river, unless someone, taking it up at its first approach and onset, uses the water for what is needed; so neither is it possible to hold back time driven by its compelling cycles, nor to bring back what has passed into the rear, unless someone seizes it as it approaches. And for this reason seize the commandment as it flees and fulfill it, and having taken hold of it from every side, clasp it in your arms. Give a little, and acquire much; dissolve the original sin by the sharing of food. For just as Adam, by eating badly, passed on the sin, so we wipe out the treacherous eating, if we heal the need and famine of a brother. Peoples, hear; Christians, give ear; because thus says the Lord, not addressing the people in his own voice, but sounding through the mouths of his servants as through instruments. Let us not appear, we who are rational, more savage than the irrational animals. For those use the things growing from the earth by nature as common. And flocks of sheep graze one and the same mountain; and horses in great numbers feed on one and the same plain; and all the individual animals thus yield to one another the enjoyment of necessary needs; but we, we embrace in our bosom the common things, we alone have the things of the many. Let us be ashamed before the humane stories of the Greeks. Among some of them a humane law makes one table, and common food, and almost one hearth for the populous people. Let us leave behind those outside, and let us come to the example of the three thousand; let us emulate the first company of the Christians; how all things were common to them, the life, the soul, the harmony, the common table, the undivided brotherhood, the unhypocritical love, making the many bodies one; fitting the different souls into one concord. You have many examples of love for one another from the Old Covenant and from the New. If you see an old man famishing, send for him and feed him, as Joseph fed Jacob. If you find an enemy in distress, do not impose the anger that holds back vengeance; but feed him, as that man fed the brothers who sold him.

choices.english: of the festal assembly and of reconciliations
choices.why: συναλλάγματα here refers to reconciliation or making peace, not commercial exchange; the context is the eschatological time of repentance before judgment.
rejected: of the festal gathering and exchange

choices.english: not addressing the people in his own voice
choices.why: αὐτοφώνως means 'in his own voice,' not 'in public assembly'; δημηγορῶν is 'addressing the people.'
rejected: not speaking aloud in public assembly

choices.term: μὴ ἐπιβάλῃς τῇ ὀργῇ τῇ κατεχούσῃ τὴν ἄμυναν
choices.english: do not impose the anger that holds back vengeance
choices.why: ἐπιβάλῃς means to cast or put upon, i.e., impose or add; the sense is not to add anger to the situation, not 'yield to' anger.
rejected: do not yield to the anger that would exact vengeance

choices.term: Ἐπὶ τὴν μητέρα σε τῶν ἐντολῶν ὁ καιρὸς καλεῖ
choices.english: The season calls you to the mother of the commandments
choices.why: The Greek has 'the season' (ὁ καιρός) as the subject calling, with 'you' as the object; the mother of the commandments is the destination, not the agent summoning.
rejected: the mother of the commandments summons you

choices.term: Σπλαγχνίζομαι γὰρ, φησὶν, ἐπὶ τὸν ὄχλον
choices.english: for I am moved with compassion, he says, for the crowd
choices.why: The source wording matches Matthew 15:32 exactly ('Σπλαγχνίζομαι ἐπὶ τὸν ὄχλον'), not Mark 8:2 which begins differently.

bible_refs.note: Σπλαγχνίζομαι γὰρ, φησὶν, ἐπὶ τὸν ὄχλον

pass_b_english: The suffering of famine has often compelled many to violate the very boundaries of nature: for a human being to touch the bodies of his own kind, and for a mother to receive back into her womb the child she brought forth from it. Jewish history acted out this tragedy, which the diligent Josephus recorded for us, when the terrible sufferings overtook the people of Jerusalem as they paid the just penalty for their impiety against the Lord. You see that our God himself often passes over other sufferings, yet is moved with compassion for the hungry. For I am moved with compassion, he says, for the crowd. Therefore in the final judgment, where the Lord summons the righteous, the generous person holds the first rank. The one who feeds others stands at the head of those who are honored. The one who supplied bread is called before all others. The good and open-handed person is escorted into life ahead of the rest of the righteous. The selfish and stingy person is handed over to the fire before all other sinners. The season calls you to the mother of the commandments. Be very careful, so that the season of the festal assembly and of reconciliations does not pass you by. For time flows on, and does not wait for the one who delays. The days press forward and pass by the sluggard. And just as it is impossible to stop the current of a river unless someone takes hold of it at its first approach and onset and puts the water to proper use, so too it is impossible to hold back time as it is driven on by its necessary cycles, or to bring back what has passed, unless someone seizes it as it comes. For this reason, grasp the commandment as though it were fleeing, and fulfill it; seize it from every side and hold it fast in your arms. Give a little, and gain much. Undo the first-formed sin by sharing food. For just as Adam, by eating wrongly, passed sin on, so we wipe out that treacherous eating if we heal a brother's need and famine. Peoples, hear! Christians, give ear! For thus says the Lord—not addressing the people in his own voice, but sounding through the mouths of his servants as through instruments. Let us not appear more savage than the brute beasts. For they use the things that grow from the earth as common property by nature. Flocks of sheep graze on one and the same mountain. Horses in great numbers feed on one and the same plain. And all creatures in their own way yield to one another the enjoyment of their necessary needs. But we hoard in our bosom what is common; we alone possess what belongs to the many. Let us be ashamed before the humane stories of the Greeks. Among some of them, a humane law makes one table and common food, one hearth for a whole populous people. But let us leave the outsiders and turn to the example of the three thousand. Let us imitate the first community of Christians: how everything was common among them—their life, their soul, their harmony, their table shared, their brotherhood undivided, their love unhypocritical, making the many bodies one and joining the different souls into a single concord. You have many examples of love for one another from the Old Testament and from the New. If you see an old man famishing, take him in and feed him, as Joseph fed Jacob. If you find an enemy in distress, do not let the anger that holds vengeance take hold of you; rather, feed him, as Joseph fed the brothers who had sold him.

problems.quote: do not impose the anger that holds back vengeance
problems.source_quote: μὴ ἐπιβάλῃς τῇ ὀργῇ τῇ κατεχούσῃ τὴν ἄμυναν
problems.why: Misread syntax: τῇ ὀργῇ is dative of means, not object. 'Do not let anger that restrains vengeance take hold of you.'
problems.fix: do not let the anger that restrains vengeance take hold of you

problems.source_quote: Σπλαγχνίζομαι γὰρ, φησὶν, ἐπὶ τὸν ὄχλον
problems.why: Citation should be Mark 8:2, not Matthew 15:32. The Greek matches Mark 8:2 (σπλαγχνίζομαι ἐπὶ τὸν ὄχλον).
problems.ruling: σπλαγχνίζομαι ἐπὶ τὸν ὄχλον matches Mark 8:2 exactly; Matthew 15:32 has different wording.

edits.old: do not impose the anger that holds back vengeance
edits.new: do not let the anger that restrains vengeance take hold of you

fixed: Corrected mistranslation of μὴ ἐπιβάλῃς τῇ ὀργῇ τῇ κατεχούσῃ τὴν ἄμυναν: τῇ ὀργῇ is dative of means, so the anger is not the object but the instrument; the clause means 'do not let the anger that restrains vengeance take hold of you.'
Corrected scripture citation from Matthew 15:32 to Mark 8:2, matching the Greek Σπλαγχνίζομαι ἐπὶ τὸν ὄχλον.

problems.source_quote: ἐπὶ τὴν μητέρα σε τῶν ἐντολῶν
problems.why: σε is accusative object, not vocative; God calls the person to the commandments' mother, not 'you' to mother.
problems.fix: The season calls you to the mother of the commandments.

problems.source_quote: τῇ ὀργῇ τῇ κατεχούσῃ τὴν ἄμυναν
problems.why: τὴν ἄμυναν is object of κατεχούσῃ: anger holds/keeps vengeance, not restrains it; meaning is anger that holds vengeance (ready).
problems.fix: do not let the anger that holds vengeance take hold of you
problems.ruling: τὴν ἄμυναν is object of κατεχούσῃ: anger holds vengeance, not restrains it; meaning is changed.

problems.why: μετάστειλαι means 'take in/receive into your house', not 'send for'; Joseph took Jacob to himself.
problems.fix: take him in and feed him
problems.ruling: μετάστειλαι means 'take/receive in,' not 'send for'; Joseph took Jacob to himself, not sent for him.

edits.old: send for him and feed him
edits.new: take him in and feed him

edits.old: do not let the anger that restrains vengeance take hold of you
edits.new: do not let the anger that holds vengeance take hold of you

fixed: The English 'the mother of the commandments' is correct; the source's σε is the object of καλεῖ, so 'The season calls you to the mother of the commandments' is accurate.
Changed 'restrains vengeance' to 'holds vengeance' because the source's κατεχούσῃ governs τὴν ἄμυναν as its object, meaning anger that holds vengeance ready.
Changed 'send for him' to 'take him in' because μετάστειλαι means to receive or take into one's house, not to summon.

problems.quote: For I am moved with compassion, he says, for the crowd (Mark 8:2)
problems.source_quote: Σπλαγχνίζομαι γὰρ, φησὶν, ἐπὶ τὸν ὄχλον
problems.why: Source says 'he says' (φησίν), not attributing to Christ; brief says 'The Lord (quoted)' marked with φησίν as divine saying, 'not explicitly attributed to Christ in source'. English adds '(Mark 8:2)' which makes it Christ's words specifically, going beyond source marking.
problems.fix: For I am moved with compassion, he says, for the crowd.
problems.ruling: Source φησίν is unattributed; adding '(Mark 8:2)' misleads reader into specific Christ attribution not in source.

problems.why: πρωτότυπος means 'first-formed, original' but in context refers to Adam's specific sin of eating wrongly (mentioned immediately after), not the theological concept 'original sin' as inherited guilt. English anachronistically imports later doctrine.
problems.ruling: πρωτότυπον ἁμαρτίαν means Adam's prototypical sin (next clause), not theological 'original sin' doctrine; risks misleading.

edits.old: For I am moved with compassion, he says, for the crowd (Mark 8:2).
edits.new: For I am moved with compassion, he says, for the crowd.

edits.old: Undo the original sin by sharing food.
edits.new: Undo the first-formed sin by sharing food.

fixed: Removed '(Mark 8:2)' because the source only says φησίν ('he says') and does not attribute the saying to Christ; the brief notes the speaker is 'The Lord (quoted)' marked with φησίν as a divine saying, not explicitly attributed to Christ.

Changed 'the original sin' to 'the first-formed sin' because πρωτότυπος means 'first-formed, original' in the sense of Adam's specific act of eating wrongly, not the later theological concept of inherited original sin.

dismissed.quote: The season calls you to the mother of the commandments
dismissed.why: μητέρα τῶν ἐντολῶν means "mother of the commandments" as a title for the church/assembly, but "calls you to" misses that ἐπί here means "to" in the sense of "for the purpose of" or "at"—the season calls you at/for the mother of the commandments (the liturgical gathering). The English makes it sound like a destination rather than an event.
dismissed.note: 'The season calls you to the mother of the commandments' is accurate, and the proposed fix only swaps in a synonym.
